units.english_question: According to the right to freedom of thought, conscience, and religion, what is a person free to change?
units.english_answer: A person is free to change his religion or belief.
units.english_passage: Everyone has the right to freedom of thought, conscience and religion; this right includes freedom to change his religion or belief, and freedom, either alone or in community with others and in public or in private, to manifest his religion or belief in teaching, practice, worship and observance. Everyone has the right to freedom of opinion and expression; this right includes freedom to hold opinions without interference and to seek, receive and impart information and ideas through any media and regardless of frontiers.
units.translation: प्रत्येक व्यक्तीस आपला धर्म वा आपला विश्वास बदलण्याचे स्वातंत्र्य आहे.

units.english_question: According to the text, for whose intangible cultural heritage must respect be ensured?
units.english_answer: Respect must be ensured for the intangible cultural heritage of the communities, groups and individuals concerned.
units.english_passage: The purposes of this Convention are: (a) to safeguard the intangible cultural heritage; (b) to ensure respect for the intangible cultural heritage of the communities, groups and individuals concerned; (c) to raise awareness at the local, national and international levels of the importance of the intangible cultural heritage, and of ensuring mutual appreciation thereof; (d) to provide for international cooperation and assistance.
units.translation: संबंधित समुदाय, गट व व्यक्ती यांच्या अमूर्त सांस्कृतिक वारशाबद्दल आदर सुनिश्चित केला पाहिजे.

units.english_question: According to the text, what is the cause of the barbarous acts that outraged the conscience of mankind?
units.english_answer: Disregard and contempt for human rights.
units.english_passage: Whereas recognition of the inherent dignity and of the equal and inalienable rights of all members of the human family is the foundation of freedom, justice and peace in the world, Whereas disregard and contempt for human rights have resulted in barbarous acts which have outraged the conscience of mankind, and the advent of a world in which human beings shall enjoy freedom of speech and belief and freedom from fear and want has been proclaimed as the highest aspiration of the common people, Whereas it is essential, if man is not to be compelled to have recourse, as a last resort, to rebellion against tyranny and oppression, that human rights should be protected by the rule of law.
units.translation: मानवी अधिकारांची अवहेलना व अपमान.

units.english_question: According to the text, what must the Union take into account in its action under other provisions of the Treaties?
units.english_answer: Cultural aspects, in particular in order to respect and promote the diversity of its cultures.
units.english_passage: The Union shall contribute to the flowering of the cultures of the Member States, while respecting their national and regional diversity and at the same time bringing the common cultural heritage to the fore. Action by the Union shall be aimed at encouraging cooperation between Member States and, if necessary, supporting and supplementing their action in the following areas: improvement of the knowledge and dissemination of the culture and history of the European peoples, conservation and safeguarding of cultural heritage of European significance, non-commercial cultural exchanges, artistic and literary creation, including in the audiovisual sector. The Union and the Member States shall foster cooperation with third countries and the competent international organisations in the sphere of culture, in particular the Council of Europe. The Union shall take cultural aspects into account in its action under other provisions of the Treaties, in particular in order to respect and to promote the diversity of its cultures.
units.translation: सांस्कृतिक बाबी, विशेषतः आपल्या संस्कृतींच्या विविधतेचा आदर करण्यासाठी व तिला प्रोत्साहन देण्यासाठी.

units.english_question: According to this text, what physical characteristics must not be used to treat someone differently?
units.english_answer: Sex, race, colour, genetic features, disability and age.
units.english_passage: Any discrimination based on any ground such as sex, race, colour, ethnic or social origin, genetic features, language, religion or belief, political or any other opinion, membership of a national minority, property, birth, disability, age or sexual orientation shall be prohibited. The Union shall respect cultural, religious and linguistic diversity.
units.translation: लिंग, वंश, वर्ण, अनुवांशिक वैशिष्ट्ये, अपंगत्व आणि वय.

units.english_question: At what three geographic or political levels must awareness of the importance of intangible cultural heritage be raised?
units.english_answer: At the local, national and international levels.
units.english_passage: The purposes of this Convention are: (a) to safeguard the intangible cultural heritage; (b) to ensure respect for the intangible cultural heritage of the communities, groups and individuals concerned; (c) to raise awareness at the local, national and international levels of the importance of the intangible cultural heritage, and of ensuring mutual appreciation thereof; (d) to provide for international cooperation and assistance.
units.translation: स्थानिक, राष्ट्रीय व आंतरराष्ट्रीय स्तरांवर.

units.english_question: From generation to generation, how is the intangible cultural heritage passed down?
units.english_answer: It is transmitted from generation to generation and constantly recreated by communities and groups in response to their environment, their interaction with nature and their history.
units.english_passage: The 'Intangible Cultural Heritage' means the practices, representations, expressions, knowledge, skills – as well as the instruments, objects, artefacts and cultural spaces associated therewith – that communities, groups and, in some cases, individuals recognize as part of their cultural heritage. This intangible cultural heritage, transmitted from generation to generation, is constantly recreated by communities and groups in response to their environment, their interaction with nature and their history, and provides them with a sense of identity and continuity, thus promoting respect for cultural diversity and human creativity.
units.translation: तो पिढ्यानपिढ्या संक्रमित केला जातो आणि समुदाय व गट आपले पर्यावरण, निसर्गाशी असलेला आपला संवाद व आपला इतिहास यांना प्रतिसाद म्हणून त्याची सतत पुनर्निर्मिती करतात.

units.english_question: How did Obatala and Olodumare cooperate in the creation of life?
units.english_answer: Obatala created the first human figurines out of earth in Ile-Ife and Olodumare breathed the breath of life into them.
units.english_passage: The Yoruba people are an ethnic group that primarily inhabits West Africa. The oldest known textual reference to the name Yoruba is found in a manuscript written by the scholar Ahmed Baba in the year 1614 in Timbuktu. The Yoruba indigenous religion is known as Isese, which encompasses traditional practices and beliefs. According to Yoruba mythology, the deity Obatala created the first human figurines out of earth in the sacred city of Ile-Ife, while the Supreme Creator, Olodumare, breathed the breath of life into them. Central to Yoruba philosophy is the concept of Omoluwabi, a guiding principle that dictates civilized behavior and good character. The term is derived from the phrase 'Omo + ti + Olu-iwa + bi', which conceptually identifies a person of exemplary virtue. An Omoluwabi demonstrates Iwapele, which signifies a set of values such as integrity, self-control, empathy, and hard work. This philosophical framework heavily influences traditional Yoruba art. Unlike Western aesthetic traditions, Yoruba art, including intricate textiles, often possesses a direct political and spiritual function, emphasizing the deep linguistic and cultural connection between visual artifacts and good moral character.
units.translation: ओबाताला याने इले-इफे येथे मातीपासून पहिल्या मानवी आकृती घडवल्या आणि ओलोदुमारे याने त्यांच्यात जीवनाचा श्वास फुंकला.

units.english_question: How does the text explain the social function of using costumes and masks?
units.english_answer: They allow people to set aside their everyday individuality and experience a heightened sense of social unity.
units.english_passage: Carnival typically involves public celebrations, including events such as parades, public street parties and other entertainments, combining some elements of a circus. Elaborate costumes and masks allow people to set aside their everyday individuality and experience a heightened sense of social unity. Participants often indulge in excessive consumption of alcohol, meat, and other foods that will be forgone during the upcoming religious season of Lent.

units.english_question: How many religions celebrate Diwali according to the text?
units.english_answer: Three.
units.english_passage: Diwali, commonly known as the festival of lights, is a Hindu festival with variations celebrated in other Indian religions such as Jainism and Sikhism. It symbolises the spiritual victory of Dharma over Adharma, light over darkness, good over evil, and knowledge over ignorance. During the festival, the celebrants illuminate their homes, temples and workspaces with diyas (oil lamps), candles and lanterns. Food is a major focus with families partaking in feasts and sharing sweets.

units.english_question: How should human beings act towards one another?
units.english_answer: They should act towards one another in a spirit of brotherhood.
units.english_passage: All human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights. They are endowed with reason and conscience and should act towards one another in a spirit of brotherhood. Everyone is entitled to all the rights and freedoms set forth in this Declaration, without distinction of any kind, such as race, colour, sex, language, religion, political or other opinion, national or social origin, property, birth or other status.
units.translation: त्यांनी एकमेकांशी बंधुत्वाच्या भावनेने आचरण करावे.

units.english_question: If a community's heritage involves astronomical observations and ecological farming methods, which domain in the text covers these activities?
units.english_answer: Domain (d), knowledge and practices concerning nature and the universe.
units.english_passage: The 'intangible cultural heritage', as defined in paragraph 1 above, is manifested inter alia in the following domains: (a) oral traditions and expressions, including language as a vehicle of the intangible cultural heritage; (b) performing arts; (c) social practices, rituals and festive events; (d) knowledge and practices concerning nature and the universe; (e) traditional craftsmanship.

units.english_question: In which stages of education must tuition or fees not be charged?
units.english_answer: In the elementary and fundamental stages.
units.english_passage: Everyone has the right to education. Education shall be free, at least in the elementary and fundamental stages. Elementary education shall be compulsory. units.english_question: On what specific calendar and date does this harvest festival occur?
units.english_answer: On the 15th day of the 8th month of the Chinese lunisolar calendar.
units.english_passage: The Mid-Autumn Festival, also known as the Moon Festival or Mooncake Festival, is a harvest festival celebrated in Chinese culture. It occurs on the 15th day of the 8th month of the Chinese lunisolar calendar. The festival celebrates three fundamental concepts that are closely connected: Gathering, such as family and friends coming together or harvesting crops; Giving thanks for the harvest or harmonious unions; and Praying for conceptual or material satisfaction, such as babies, a spouse, beauty, longevity, or a good future.

units.english_question: Through what channels and boundaries can information and ideas be sought, received, and imparted?
units.english_answer: Information and ideas can be sought, received and imparted through any media and regardless of frontiers.

units.english_question: Under what condition might a person be forced to rebel against tyranny and oppression as a last resort?
units.english_answer: If human rights are not protected by the rule of law.
units.english_passage: Whereas recognition of the inherent dignity and of the equal and inalienable rights of all members of the human family is the foundation of freedom, justice and peace in the world, Whereas disregard and contempt for human rights have resulted in barbarous acts which have outraged the conscience of mankind, and the advent of a world in which human beings shall enjoy freedom of speech and belief and freedom from fear and want has been proclaimed as the highest aspiration of the common people, Whereas it is essential, if man is not to be compelled to have recourse, as a last resort, to rebellion against tyranny and oppression, that human rights should be protected by the rule of law.
units.translation: जर कायद्याच्या राज्याकडून मानवी अधिकारांचे संरक्षण केले गेले नाही तर.

units.english_question: What actions can fuel hostility and hinder post-conflict national healing, other than destruction, looting and smuggling?
units.english_answer: The attempt to deny historical roots and cultural diversity.
units.english_passage: Emphasizing that the unlawful destruction of cultural heritage, and the looting and smuggling of cultural property in the event of armed conflicts, notably by terrorist groups, and the attempt to deny historical roots and cultural diversity in this context can fuel and exacerbate conflict and hamper post-conflict reconciliation, thereby undermining the security, stability, governance, social cohesion and development of affected Member States.

units.english_question: What are the availability and accessibility requirements for technical and professional education compared to higher education?
units.english_answer: Technical and professional education shall be made generally available, while higher education shall be equally accessible to all on the basis of merit.

units.english_question: What are two alternative names for the Mid-Autumn Festival?
units.english_answer: The Moon Festival and the Mooncake Festival.

units.english_answer: Religion or belief, and political or any other opinion.

units.english_question: What causes the grave threats to intangible cultural heritage in particular?
units.english_answer: A lack of resources for safeguarding such heritage.

units.english_question: What does the style of Wabi-cha emphasize?
units.english_answer: Simplicity.
units.english_passage: Wabi-cha is a style of Japanese tea ceremony particularly associated with Sen no Rikyu, Takeno Joo and its originator Murata Juko. Wabi-cha emphasizes simplicity. The term came into use in the Edo period, prior to which it was known as wabi-suki, suki meaning 'artistic inclination', and 'wabi' meaning 'forlorn'. At the core of Rikyu's aesthetic was the tea room smaller than 4.5 tatami mats, which was a practical way of focusing tea practice on the communion of host and guests.

units.english_question: What five specific purposes of dedicated sites and buildings are protected from attacks under this article?
units.english_answer: Religion, education, art, science and charitable purposes.
units.english_passage: Affirms that directing unlawful attacks against sites and buildings dedicated to religion, education, art, science or charitable purposes, or historic monuments may constitute, under certain circumstances and pursuant to international law, a war crime and that perpetrators of such attacks must be brought to justice.

units.english_question: What has everyone the right to freely participate in?
units.english_answer: The cultural life of the community.

units.translation: समाजाच्या सांस्कृतिक जीवनात.

units.english_question: What is the definition of 'intangible cultural heritage'?
units.english_answer: It means the practices, representations, expressions, knowledge and skills, as well as the instruments, objects, artefacts and cultural spaces associated with them, that communities, groups and sometimes individuals recognize as part of their cultural heritage.
units.english_passage: The 'Intangible Cultural Heritage' means the practices, representations, expressions, knowledge, skills – as well as the instruments, objects, artefacts and cultural spaces associated therewith – that communities, groups and, in some cases, individuals recognize as part of their cultural heritage. This intangible cultural heritage, transmitted from generation to generation, is constantly recreated by communities and groups in response to their environment, their interaction with nature and their history, and provides them with a sense of identity and continuity, thus promoting respect for cultural diversity and human creativity.

The Union and the Member States shall foster cooperation with third countries and the competent international organisations in the sphere of culture, in particular the Council of Europe. The Union shall take cultural aspects into account in its action under other provisions of the Treaties, in particular in order to respect and to promote the diversity of its cultures.

units.english_question: What region do these AI practices apply to?
units.english_answer: The European Union.
units.english_passage: The following artificial intelligence (AI) practices shall be prohibited in the European Union: (a) the placing on the market, the putting into service or the use of an AI system that deploys subliminal techniques beyond a person’s consciousness or purposefully manipulative or deceptive techniques, with the objective or the effect of materially distorting a person’s behaviour by appreciably impairing the person’s ability to make an informed decision, thereby causing or being likely to cause that person or another person significant harm; (b) the placing on the market, the putting into service or the use of an AI system that exploits any of the vulnerabilities of a person or a specific group of persons due to their age, disability or a specific social or economic situation, with the objective or the effect of materially distorting the behaviour of that person or a person belonging to that group in a manner that causes or is reasonably likely to cause that person or another person significant harm; (c) the placing on the market, the putting into service or the use of AI systems for the evaluation or classification of natural persons over a certain period of time based on their social behaviour or known, inferred or predicted personal or personality characteristics, with the social score leading to detrimental or unfavourable treatment; (d) the placing on the market, the putting into service or the use of an AI system for making risk assessments of natural persons in order to assess or predict the likelihood of a natural person committing a criminal offence, based solely on the profiling of a natural person or on assessing their personality traits and characteristics.

units.english_question: What three specific actions regarding AI systems are prohibited?
units.english_answer: Placing on the market, putting into service, and use.
units.english_passage: The following artificial intelligence (AI) practices shall be prohibited in the European Union: (a) the placing on the market, the putting into service or the use of an AI system that deploys subliminal techniques beyond a person’s consciousness or purposefully manipulative or deceptive techniques, with the objective or the effect of materially distorting a person’s behaviour by appreciably impairing the person’s ability to make an informed decision, thereby causing or being likely to cause that person or another person significant harm; (b) the placing on the market, the putting into service or the use of an AI system that exploits any of the vulnerabilities of a person or a specific group of persons due to their age, disability or a specific social or economic situation, with the objective or the effect of materially distorting the behaviour of that person or a person belonging to that group in a manner that causes or is reasonably likely to cause that person or another person significant harm; (c) the placing on the market, the putting into service or the use of AI systems for the evaluation or classification of natural persons over a certain period of time based on their social behaviour or known, inferred or predicted personal or personality characteristics, with the social score leading to detrimental or unfavourable treatment; (d) the placing on the market, the putting into service or the use of an AI system for making risk assessments of natural persons in order to assess or predict the likelihood of a natural person committing a criminal offence, based solely on the profiling of a natural person or on assessing their personality traits and characteristics.
units.translation: बाजारात आणणे, सेवेत दाखल करणे आणि वापर करणे.

units.english_question: What three types of danger threaten intangible cultural heritage according to the text?
units.english_answer: Deterioration, disappearance and destruction.
units.english_passage: Recognizing that the processes of globalization and social transformation, alongside the conditions they create for renewed dialogue among communities, also give rise, as does the phenomenon of intolerance, to grave threats of deterioration, disappearance and destruction of the intangible cultural heritage, in particular because of a lack of resources for safeguarding such heritage.
units.translation: ऱ्हास, लोप व नाश.

units.english_question: What three types of diversity must the Union respect?
units.english_answer: Cultural, religious and linguistic diversity.
units.english_passage: Any discrimination based on any ground such as sex, race, colour, ethnic or social origin, genetic features, language, religion or belief, political or any other opinion, membership of a national minority, property, birth, disability, age or sexual orientation shall be prohibited. The Union shall respect cultural, religious and linguistic diversity.
units.translation: सांस्कृतिक, धार्मिक व भाषिक विविधता.

units.english_question: What two actions are unlawful other than destruction?
units.english_answer: Looting and smuggling.
units.english_passage: Deplores and condemns the unlawful destruction of cultural heritage, inter alia destruction of religious sites and artefacts, as well as the looting and smuggling of cultural property from archaeological sites, museums, libraries, archives, and other sites, in the context of armed conflicts, notably by terrorist groups.
units.translation: लूट व तस्करी.

units.english_question: What type of structures, other than functional buildings, are mentioned as potential targets?
units.english_answer: Historic monuments.
units.english_passage: Affirms that directing unlawful attacks against sites and buildings dedicated to religion, education, art, science or charitable purposes, or historic monuments may constitute, under certain circumstances and pursuant to international law, a war crime and that perpetrators of such attacks must be brought to justice.
units.translation: ऐतिहासिक स्मारके.

units.english_question: What was the size of the tea room at the core of Rikyu's aesthetic?
units.english_answer: Smaller than 4.5 tatami mats.
units.english_passage: Wabi-cha is a style of Japanese tea ceremony particularly associated with Sen no Rikyu, Takeno Joo and its originator Murata Juko. Wabi-cha emphasizes simplicity. The term came into use in the Edo period, prior to which it was known as wabi-suki, suki meaning 'artistic inclination', and 'wabi' meaning 'forlorn'. At the core of Rikyu's aesthetic was the tea room smaller than 4.5 tatami mats, which was a practical way of focusing tea practice on the communion of host and guests.
units.translation: साडेचार तातामी चटयांपेक्षा लहान.

units.english_question: When and by whom are these acts of looting and destruction notably committed?
units.english_answer: In the context of armed conflicts, notably by terrorist groups.
units.english_passage: Deplores and condemns the unlawful destruction of cultural heritage, inter alia destruction of religious sites and artefacts, as well as the looting and smuggling of cultural property from archaeological sites, museums, libraries, archives, and other sites, in the context of armed conflicts, notably by terrorist groups.
units.translation: सशस्त्र संघर्षांच्या संदर्भात, विशेषतः दहशतवादी गटांकडून.

units.english_question: When are unlawful attacks against sites and buildings considered war crimes?
units.english_answer: Under certain circumstances and pursuant to international law.
units.english_passage: Affirms that directing unlawful attacks against sites and buildings dedicated to religion, education, art, science or charitable purposes, or historic monuments may constitute, under certain circumstances and pursuant to international law, a war crime and that perpetrators of such attacks must be brought to justice.
units.translation: विशिष्ट परिस्थितींमध्ये आणि आंतरराष्ट्रीय कायद्यानुसार.

units.english_question: Where do the Yoruba people live?
units.english_answer: They primarily inhabit West Africa.
units.english_passage: The Yoruba people are an ethnic group that primarily inhabits West Africa. The oldest known textual reference to the name Yoruba is found in a manuscript written by the scholar Ahmed Baba in the year 1614 in Timbuktu. The Yoruba indigenous religion is known as Isese, which encompasses traditional practices and beliefs. According to Yoruba mythology, the deity Obatala created the first human figurines out of earth in the sacred city of Ile-Ife, while the Supreme Creator, Olodumare, breathed the breath of life into them. Central to Yoruba philosophy is the concept of Omoluwabi, a guiding principle that dictates civilized behavior and good character. The term is derived from the phrase 'Omo + ti + Olu-iwa + bi', which conceptually identifies a person of exemplary virtue. An Omoluwabi demonstrates Iwapele, which signifies a set of values such as integrity, self-control, empathy, and hard work. This philosophical framework heavily influences traditional Yoruba art. Unlike Western aesthetic traditions, Yoruba art, including intricate textiles, often possesses a direct political and spiritual function, emphasizing the deep linguistic and cultural connection between visual artifacts and good moral character.
units.translation: ते प्रामुख्याने पश्चिम आफ्रिकेत राहतात.

units.english_question: Which Japanese word is tied to feeling left behind or separated from someone you care about?
units.english_answer: Wabi, meaning 'forlorn'.
units.english_passage: Wabi-cha is a style of Japanese tea ceremony particularly associated with Sen no Rikyu, Takeno Joo and its originator Murata Juko. Wabi-cha emphasizes simplicity. The term came into use in the Edo period, prior to which it was known as wabi-suki, suki meaning 'artistic inclination', and 'wabi' meaning 'forlorn'. At the core of Rikyu's aesthetic was the tea room smaller than 4.5 tatami mats, which was a practical way of focusing tea practice on the communion of host and guests.
units.translation: वाबी, ज्याचा अर्थ एकाकी असा होतो.

units.english_question: Which economic and birth-related factors are listed that must not be used to deny rights?
units.english_answer: Property and birth.
units.english_passage: All human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights. They are endowed with reason and conscience and should act towards one another in a spirit of brotherhood. Everyone is entitled to all the rights and freedoms set forth in this Declaration, without distinction of any kind, such as race, colour, sex, language, religion, political or other opinion, national or social origin, property, birth or other status.
units.translation: मालमत्ता व जन्म.

units.english_question: Which international organisation is highlighted for cultural cooperation with the Union and Member States?
units.english_answer: The Council of Europe.
units.english_passage: The Union shall contribute to the flowering of the cultures of the Member States, while respecting their national and regional diversity and at the same time bringing the common cultural heritage to the fore. Action by the Union shall be aimed at encouraging cooperation between Member States and, if necessary, supporting and supplementing their action in the following areas: improvement of the knowledge and dissemination of the culture and history of the European peoples, conservation and safeguarding of cultural heritage of European significance, non-commercial cultural exchanges, artistic and literary creation, including in the audiovisual sector. The Union and the Member States shall foster cooperation with third countries and the competent international organisations in the sphere of culture, in particular the Council of Europe. The Union shall take cultural aspects into account in its action under other provisions of the Treaties, in particular in order to respect and to promote the diversity of its cultures.
units.translation: युरोप परिषद.

units.english_question: Which levels of cultural diversity will be respected by the Union?
units.english_answer: National and regional diversity.
units.english_passage: The Union shall contribute to the flowering of the cultures of the Member States, while respecting their national and regional diversity and at the same time bringing the common cultural heritage to the fore. Action by the Union shall be aimed at encouraging cooperation between Member States and, if necessary, supporting and supplementing their action in the following areas: improvement of the knowledge and dissemination of the culture and history of the European peoples, conservation and safeguarding of cultural heritage of European significance, non-commercial cultural exchanges, artistic and literary creation, including in the audiovisual sector. The Union and the Member States shall foster cooperation with third countries and the competent international organisations in the sphere of culture, in particular the Council of Europe. The Union shall take cultural aspects into account in its action under other provisions of the Treaties, in particular in order to respect and to promote the diversity of its cultures.
units.translation: राष्ट्रीय व प्रादेशिक विविधता.

units.english_question: Which other activity is listed under section (c) alongside social practices and rituals?
units.english_answer: Festive events.
units.english_passage: The 'intangible cultural heritage', as defined in paragraph 1 above, is manifested inter alia in the following domains: (a) oral traditions and expressions, including language as a vehicle of the intangible cultural heritage; (b) performing arts; (c) social practices, rituals and festive events; (d) knowledge and practices concerning nature and the universe; (e) traditional craftsmanship.
units.translation: उत्सवप्रसंग.

units.english_question: Which purpose of this convention is broken if one of the member states is flooded, its archives destroyed, and the neighboring members stand idly by?
units.english_answer: Purpose (d), to provide for international cooperation and assistance.
units.english_passage: The purposes of this Convention are: (a) to safeguard the intangible cultural heritage; (b) to ensure respect for the intangible cultural heritage of the communities, groups and individuals concerned; (c) to raise awareness at the local, national and international levels of the importance of the intangible cultural heritage, and of ensuring mutual appreciation thereof; (d) to provide for international cooperation and assistance.
units.translation: उद्देश (ड), आंतरराष्ट्रीय सहकार्य व साहाय्य पुरवणे.

units.english_question: Which stage of education is described as compulsory?
units.english_answer: Elementary education.
units.english_passage: Everyone has the right to education. Education shall be free, at least in the elementary and fundamental stages. Elementary education shall be compulsory. Technical and professional education shall be made generally available and higher education shall be equally accessible to all on the basis of merit.
units.translation: प्राथमिक शिक्षण.

units.english_question: Which tangible pieces of art are mentioned in the passage?
units.english_answer: Intricate textiles.

units.english_question: Which three historical figures are associated with Wabi-cha, and which one of them created the style?
units.english_answer: Sen no Rikyu, Takeno Joo and Murata Juko, of whom Murata Juko was the originator.

units.translation: सेन नो रिक्यू, ताकेनो जोओ आणि मुराता जुको, ज्यांपैकी मुराता जुको हा या शैलीचा जनक होता.

units.english_question: Who in particular is highlighted as carrying out these acts?
units.english_answer: Terrorist groups.
units.english_passage: Emphasizing that the unlawful destruction of cultural heritage, and the looting and smuggling of cultural property in the event of armed conflicts, notably by terrorist groups, and the attempt to deny historical roots and cultural diversity in this context can fuel and exacerbate conflict and hamper post-conflict reconciliation, thereby undermining the security, stability, governance, social cohesion and development of affected Member States.
units.translation: दहशतवादी गट.

units.english_question: Who is entitled to the legal protection of the creative and financial interests of a production under this text?
units.english_answer: The author of the production.
units.english_passage: Everyone has the right freely to participate in the cultural life of the community, to enjoy the arts and to share in scientific advancement and its benefits. Everyone has the right to the protection of the moral and material interests resulting from any scientific, literary or artistic production of which he is the author.
units.translation: त्या कृतीचा निर्माता.

units.english_question: Why can't Danish police use AI to predict future tax evasion?
units.english_answer: Because point (d) prohibits AI systems that assess or predict the likelihood of a person committing a criminal offence based solely on profiling or personality traits.

units.translation: कारण मुद्दा (ड) अशा एआय प्रणालींना प्रतिबंध करतो, ज्या केवळ व्यक्तीच्या प्रोफाइलिंगच्या किंवा तिच्या व्यक्तिमत्त्वाच्या वैशिष्ट्यांच्या आधारे ती व्यक्ती गुन्हा करण्याची शक्यता किती आहे याचे मूल्यांकन किंवा भाकीत करतात.

units.english_question: Why can't an insurance company use AI to determine an insurance premium?
units.english_answer: Because point (c) prohibits evaluating or classifying people over time on the basis of social behaviour or personal characteristics where the resulting score leads to detrimental or unfavourable treatment.
units.english_passage: The following artificial intelligence (AI) practices shall be prohibited in the European Union: (a) the placing on the market, the putting into service or the use of an AI system that deploys subliminal techniques beyond a person’s consciousness or purposefully manipulative or deceptive techniques, with the objective or the effect of materially distorting a person’s behaviour by appreciably impairing the person’s ability to make an informed decision, thereby causing or being likely to cause that person or another person significant harm; (b) the placing on the market, the putting into service or the use of an AI system that exploits any of the vulnerabilities of a person or a specific group of persons due to their age, disability or a specific social or economic situation, with the objective or the effect of materially distorting the behaviour of that person or a person belonging to that group in a manner that causes or is reasonably likely to cause that person or another person significant harm; (c) the placing on the market, the putting into service or the use of AI systems for the evaluation or classification of natural persons over a certain period of time based on their social behaviour or known, inferred or predicted personal or personality characteristics, with the social score leading to detrimental or unfavourable treatment; (d) the placing on the market, the putting into service or the use of an AI system for making risk assessments of natural persons in order to assess or predict the likelihood of a natural person committing a criminal offence, based solely on the profiling of a natural person or on assessing their personality traits and characteristics.
units.translation: कारण मुद्दा (क) सामाजिक वर्तनाच्या किंवा वैयक्तिक वैशिष्ट्यांच्या आधारे ठराविक कालावधीत व्यक्तींचे मूल्यांकन किंवा वर्गीकरण करण्यास प्रतिबंध करतो, जेव्हा त्यातून मिळणाऱ्या गुणांकामुळे हानिकारक किंवा प्रतिकूल वागणूक मिळते.

units.english_question: With what internal faculties are all human beings endowed at birth?
units.english_answer: Reason and conscience.
units.english_passage: All human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights. They are endowed with reason and conscience and should act towards one another in a spirit of brotherhood. Everyone is entitled to all the rights and freedoms set forth in this Declaration, without distinction of any kind, such as race, colour, sex, language, religion, political or other opinion, national or social origin, property, birth or other status.
